source.title: Induction Heads Interpolate N-Grams
source.authors: Francesco D'Angelo; Oğuz Kaan Yüksel; S. Narashiman; Nicolas Flammarion

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests induction-head computation on synthetic Markov-chain tasks using a soft-context-matching analysis and trained-model attention visualizations. It does not reproduce the original training-time phase-change and loss-curve measurement.
record.gate_note: The paper also discusses phase formation and data properties in cited work, but those cited results are not rows. Its own attention-pattern and prediction results are recorded below; the plotted KL values are not numerically stated in the text.
record.test_reason: The paper trains two-layer transformers on order-2 Markov chains. It checks whether they learn the induction circuit: lag-1 and lag-2 copy (previous-token) heads in layer 1 feeding a layer-2 head that matches the current context against earlier contexts and aggregates their successor tokens. It does this with attention maps and weight matrices, a different method from the original training-dynamics study. This bears on V1 (mechanism, in the attention-only disentangled model) and narrowly on V4 (a standard transformer with LayerNorm and MLP learns the same circuit). It does not measure formation timing, loss bumps, large-model ICL or few-shot tasks.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors also conclude that trained models approach the Bayes-optimal add-α predictor when pseudo-count smoothing is optimal, and beat fixed add-α baselines under the hierarchical prior. Their framing is that induction heads regularize in-context estimation rather than merely count exact matches.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a two-layer copy-and-match circuit and trained-model attention analyses on synthetic Markov chains. Emphasizes finite-scale soft matching and BOS pseudo-counts rather than training-time emergence, loss bumps, or broad language-model behavior.
record.method_sensitivity: The learned estimator and performance vary with task prior (independent versus hierarchical Dirichlet), BOS presence, and attention-weight scale; the hierarchical prior yields asymmetric matching weights favoring the most-recent token.

fits_no_version.finding: The estimator the induction head implements depends on task prior and BOS. With the independent prior plus BOS it matches exactly and uses BOS as pseudo-counts. Without BOS, or under the hierarchical prior, it spreads attention over partial matches. Under the hierarchical prior it weights lag-1 above lag-2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The statistical estimator realised by induction heads (pseudo-count smoothing vs. interpolation across context orders) adapts to the data prior and to structural tokens like BOS.

record.problems: The empirical tasks are synthetic Markov chains with order k = 2 and vocabulary size 5. The paper states that theoretical guarantees cover the disentangled two-layer architecture; evidence for standard transformers is from experiments. KL curves are presented in figures without exact values or reported uncertainty. The authors leave deeper stacks, large-scale models, and natural text for future work.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results left out.

untested.parts: How the circuit forms during training (composition dynamics). In the no-BOS run, Layer 1 was initialized to copy heads.
All of it: no training-time formation window, ICL jump or loss bump is measured.
All of it: no large models and no loss-by-token-index attribution.
Model sizes beyond two layers, other model families, natural text, other modalities. Training-run variation: 3 seeds were run but only the converged seed is shown.
Whether or when heads form as data or setup vary. Heads form in every tested condition.
All of it: no training trajectory is analysed.

missing.what: Hierarchical runs cover 9 sequence lengths (T from 32 to 1024) and 3 seeds, but only the converged T=128 and T=32 models are shown. Consistency across seeds and lengths is not reported.
The no-BOS trained model had Layer 1 initialized to hard copy heads, which affects whether previous-token head formation was learned.
Main-text direct evidence that trained models reproduce the construction's attention patterns on the independent task, for both interpolation and BOS variants.

record.verdict_notes: The KL rows (R6–R10) measure predictive quality against baselines, not induction-head presence or formation, so they are unlinked. The reader's V5 labels are dropped because formation was never varied; the data dependence of the estimator goes under fits_no_version. The reader's V4 limits_scope label is replaced by untested parts, since narrow coverage is not a qualification. Evidence is qualitative (attention maps), with no numeric attention values or uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: The paper constructs and observes a two-layer copy-and-match circuit, but does not specifically test formation by composing with a previous-token head as described in the version.
No training-time induction-head formation window, abrupt transition, in-context-learning loss-by-token-index gain, or training-loss bump is measured.
The study does not test whether induction heads carry most ICL in large transformers or measure loss falling with token index in large models.
Tests disentangled and standard two-layer transformers on synthetic Markov tasks, but not a broad range of model families, sizes, training runs, architectures, or modalities.
Varies task prior and BOS setup and reports resulting mechanisms and prediction performance; does not test when heads form during training or whether ICL persists across training setups.
Does not compare few-shot task learning with token-copying behavior or test whether other mechanisms carry most few-shot learning.
Does not track circuit sub-steps or transitions during training.

rows.subject: two-layer disentangled transformer (Proposition 3.1 construction)
rows.size_stated: two layers; k attention heads in layer 1 and one attention head in layer 2
rows.operation_detail: Constructs a circuit that copies context tokens in layer 1 and uses layer 2 to match candidate contexts and aggregate their successor tokens.
rows.measure: Whether the circuit implements exact and partial context matching
rows.baseline: Hard-attention limit gives exact k-gram counting
rows.value: The proposition states that finite attention weights implement a weighted estimator over context-match masks, aggregating successor tokens with weights exponential in overlap.
rows.note: This is a constructed mechanism, not evidence about spontaneous formation during training.
rows.check: Proposition 3.1 is a hand-set weight construction, an existence proof. It is not a measurement of a trained model and should not count as evidence that the mechanism arises.

rows.subject: Disentangled Trained
rows.size_stated: two-layer disentangled architecture; other size not stated
rows.operation_detail: Visualizes learned attention and weights after training on the independent Dirichlet task.
rows.measure: Layer-1 copy attention and layer-2 attention over full and partial context matches
rows.value: The text states that the trained model implements soft context matching, distributing attention over both full and partial matches, and recovers the lag-specific copy and block-shift structure.
rows.note: The paper describes the attention pattern qualitatively; no numeric attention values are reported in the text.
rows.check: Appendix C.2 says this no-BOS trained model had Layer 1 initialized to hard copy heads (trainable). So the previous-token heads were not learned from scratch here, which conflicts with the main-text claim of full training from initialization. The layer-2 head attends to full and partial matches, not only exact [A][B]…[A] matches. Not linked to V5: formation was not varied.

rows.measure: Layer-1 lag-copy heads, layer-2 context matching, and attention across full and partial matches
rows.value: The text states that the trained model has lag-specific copy heads and layer-2 soft context matching; it assigns attention to both full and partial matches, including when BOS is present.
rows.note: The paper also reports that the learned lag-1 matching block has larger magnitude than the lag-2 block.
rows.check: Copy heads at lag 1 and lag 2 plus layer-2 context matching, learned with all parameters trainable. Mass is spread over full and partial matches, and lag-1 is weighted above lag-2. The V5 link is removed: the data prior changes the estimator's weighting, not whether or when the heads form (see fits_no_version).
